jobs.title: Director Data Platform Governance
jobs.description:
Director Data Platform Governance
Toronto, Canada (Hybrid)
Full Time

Position Overview
The Director of Data Platform Governance is responsible for establishing, operating, and continuously improving the Digital Technology governance capabilities that ensure Enterprise Data Platform and related governance tooling ecosystem are controlled, integrated, secure, scalable, traceable, and fit for enterprise use. This includes platform governance standards, certified EDP table usage, metadata, catalog, lineage, data quality monitoring, lifecycle controls, automation, bots, agents, and other tools and services that support governed data creation, certification, publication, and consumption.
The role provides DT leadership for the technical enablement, enterprise integration, architecture and security alignment, platform controls, and operational reliability of this tooling ecosystem. SimpleMDG is a key Data Governance capability sitting on top of SAP, and the Director ensures it is integrated and governed consistently with EDP, SAP, downstream platforms, and other governance-enabling tools across the enterprise technology landscape. The Director also works closely with Technology Architects to ensure proper data flow, lineage, traceability, and integration patterns across the Enterprise Data Platform.
The Director works in close alignment with Business Transformation Data Governance through a shared agenda, agreed priorities, and clear ownership boundaries. Business Transformation Data Governance and business data owners remain accountable for business definitions, semantic layer, approval workflow design, mandatory business rules, reference data certification, stewardship logic, and business adoption, while DT ensures those decisions can be embedded consistently across platforms, workflows, tools, certified data assets, data products, and consumption layers.

Key Responsibilities

1. Enterprise Data Platform Governance and Certified Data Consumption
Establish, operate, and continuously improve DT governance standards for the Enterprise Data Platform, ensuring that data products are created and consumed using certified EDP tables where available.
Define platform-level controls, metadata, lineage, traceability, catalog, and data product governance expectations for EDP assets and consumption layers.
Partner with Business Data Governance and DT delivery teams to embed certified data consumption, lineage, controls, and governance checkpoints into delivery standards and ways of working.
Work with Technology Architects to ensure proper data flow, integration patterns, certified consumption paths, lineage, and traceability across the Enterprise Data Platform.
2. Governance Tooling Ecosystem Enablement
Provide DT leadership for the implementation, integration, controls, security, scalability, and operational reliability of the governance tooling ecosystem, including SimpleMDG, metadata and catalog solutions, lineage tools, data quality monitoring, automation, bots, agents, and related platform services.
Ensure governance tools are connected appropriately across SAP, EDP, downstream platforms, workflows, and consumption layers so that business-approved governance decisions can be executed consistently.
Maintain clear ownership boundaries by enabling business-led configuration decisions while ensuring the technical design, integration, access, auditability, and sustainability of the tools.
3. Master Data Platform Enablement and Enterprise Integration
Support business-led master data governance model by ensuring master data capabilities are technically enabled, integrated, secure, scalable, and aligned with enterprise architecture and data platform standards.
Ensure governed and certified master data can be integrated, exposed, monitored, and consumed appropriately across SAP, SimpleMDG, EDP, downstream enterprise applications, and certified data products.
Maintain lineage, traceability, metadata, issue visibility, platform controls, and certified consumption paths for master data from source systems through EDP and downstream usage.
4. Data Quality Monitoring, Controls, and Issue Visibility
Enable data quality monitoring, profiling, dashboards, scorecards, preventative controls, and issue visibility across EDP and related governance tooling.
Ensure business-defined rules, thresholds, and quality expectations can be technically implemented, measured, and monitored across platforms and consumption layers.
Partner with BT Data Governance, business stewards, Data Product Owners, and DT teams to support root-cause analysis, remediation tracking, and continuous improvement of data quality controls.
5. Metadata, Catalog, Lineage, and Data Intelligence
Establish and operate technical metadata, catalog, lineage, discovery, classification, and transparency capabilities for EDP and related data assets.
Ensure BT-owned business definitions, glossary content, critical data elements, and certification decisions are made visible and usable through platform tools, catalogs, workflows, and data products.
Work with Technology Architects and EDP teams to maintain end-to-end lineage and traceability from source systems through certified EDP tables, data products, and consumption layers.
6. Data Lifecycle, Archiving Governance, Retention, and Platform Compliance Controls
Operate technical lifecycle, data archiving governance, retention, archival, disposition, and compliance controls for EDP and related data platforms in alignment with enterprise policy, legal, regulatory, audit, and information governance requirements.
Ensure enterprise data remains manageable, controlled, compliant, traceable, and cost-efficient throughout its lifecycle, including active use, retention, archiving, and disposition across platform and consumption layers.

Required Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Supply Chain, or related discipline.
• 12+ years of progressive experience in Data Management, Data Platforms, Master Data Management, or Enterprise Information Management
• 5+ years leading data platform or MDM organizations.
• Strong expertise in SAP Master Data structures and business processes.
• Hands-on experience implementing and operating SAP MDG and/or SimpleMDG.
• Experience leading enterprise data quality initiatives.
• Experience enabling governance operating models and stewardship programs through platform capabilities
• Strong understanding of ERP transformation programs.
• Experience managing enterprise-scale cross-functional initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications
The ideal candidate demonstrates strong expertise in:

• Enterprise Data Platform governance, including certified data assets, governed consumption layers, platform standards, controls, and auditability.
• Data product and certified consumption governance, including ownership visibility, certification practices, guardrails, and governance checkpoints across data products and analytics use cases.
• Metadata, catalog, lineage, and data intelligence capabilities, including traceability, classification, discovery, and transparency across source systems, EDP, data products, and consumption layers.
• Data quality monitoring and control frameworks, including profiling, dashboards, scorecards, preventative controls, issue visibility, and remediation tracking.
• SAP, SimpleMDG/SAP MDG, and master data platform enablement, including integration across SAP, EDP, enterprise applications, analytics platforms, and downstream consumption layers.
• Enterprise integration and lifecycle governance, including source-to-consumption data flows, integration patterns, retention, archiving, compliance, and platform controls.
• Governance-enabling tooling and enterprise transformation, including workflow automation, bots, agents, metadata/catalog tools, lineage tools, data quality platforms, ERP transformation, and enterprise-scale data platform change.
• Critical enterprise data domains and operating models, including supply chain, customer, commercial, and other core data domains, with clear distinction between business-owned governance decisions and DT-owned platform enablement.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

• Pragmatic execution, solves complex business and data problems and turns governance concepts into measurable results.
• Business process orientation, understands how trusted data supports operational execution, performance, analytics, and decision-making.
• Enterprise mindset, connects platform governance, certified data consumption, and data quality to business outcomes and transformation priorities.
• Influential leadership, builds alignment across Business Transformation, Digital Technology, Data Product Owners, architects, and senior stakeholders.
• Change and adoption focus, drives practical adoption of governance standards, platform controls, tooling, and ways of working.
• Continuous improvement discipline, improves data quality, platform reliability, governance effectiveness, and operational efficiency.

Show less

Seniority level

Director

Employment type

Full-time

Industries

IT Services and IT Consulting

jobs.title: Director Enterprise Technology Architecture
jobs.description:
Position Summary

McGill University is seeking a Director Enterprise Technology Architecture, reporting to the Senior Director, IT Governance & Strategic Planning (GSP) to lead the e nterprise technology architecture strategy and roadmap, leading enterprise-wide architecture integration, architecture principles, standards, business capabilities and governance processes while promoting innovation, business value realization, operational efficiency, and sustainable growth.

The Director of Enterprise Architecture will play a strategic role between business strategy and technology directions
guiding the organization over the long term, from broad enterprise visions to solution-level decisions.
This role serves as a trusted and strategic advisor to business and technology leaders, ensuring that technology investments and transformation initiatives, are delivered toward a coherent target sate. This role is part of a transformation context: redefining the architecture operating model to increase the autonomy of delivery teams and establish the standards to support the growth and changes.
Key Responsibilities

Strategic Enterprise Architecture

Influence enterprise technology portfolio and investment planning by assessing strategic alignment, architectural fit, enterprise reuse opportunities, dependencies, technical debt implications, and long-term sustainability of proposed investments.
Develop and evolve the organization's business and enterprise architecture strategy, ensuring alignment with the institution vision, strategic priorities, and operational objectives.
Translate institutional strategy into target-state architectures, strategic architecture priorities, and actionable transformation roadmaps.
Develop integrated business and technology roadmaps that guide organizational transformation, investment planning, and modernization priorities.
Advise senior leadership on technology investments, enterprise capabilities, architectural implications, and transformation opportunities.
Shape architecture direction for strategic domains such as AI, data, application modernization, platforms, integration, and emerging technologies.
Guide application and platform rationalization to reduce redundancy, complexity, technical debt, and operational costs.
Establish and evolve enterprise business capability and value-chain models to support strategic planning, investment prioritization, and transformation.
Define enterprise reference architectures and target-state architecture that provide strategic direction for technology capabilities, platforms, and solution design.
Communicate enterprise architecture direction, outcomes, and value to executive leadership and key stakeholders.

Business and Technology Alignment

Act as a strategic partner between business and technology leadership, ensuring technology priorities and architecture decisions support institutional objectives.
Engage business and technology leaders to understand strategic needs, emerging priorities, and transformation opportunities, and translate them into architecture requirements and priorities.
Facilitate cross-functional alignment on business capabilities, technology direction, dependencies, and architectural trade-offs.
Partner with business and technology stakeholders to align initiatives and investment priorities with enterprise roadmaps and target-state architecture.
Provide architecture guidance to programs and delivery teams, ensuring business intent is effectively translated into scalable and sustainable technology solutions.
Identify and resolve gaps or conflicts between business priorities, technology strategies, and enterprise architecture direction.

Governance and Leadership

Establish and lead enterprise-wide architecture governance to drive consistent adoption of standards, patterns, decision frameworks, reference architectures, to enable strategic technology direction across business and technology domains.
Chair the Architecture Review Boards and other governance forums, ensuring effective architectural decision-making and cross-functional alignment.
Ensure strategic initiatives, programs, and solutions align with enterprise architecture standards, target-state architectures, and approved technology direction.
Stay abreast of industry trends, emerging technologies, market developments, and architectural best practices to inform enterprise architecture direction and decision-making.
Build strong relationships with executives, business leaders, delivery teams, and technology stakeholders to strengthen architecture influence and organizational alignment.
Foster a culture of collaboration, innovation, architectural discipline, and continuous improvement.
Lead, mentor, and develop architecture practitioners while strengthening enterprise architecture capabilities, practices, and competencies across the organization.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related discipline.
Master’s degree in business administration (MBA) or relevant post-graduate studies in business is considered an asset.
Knowledge of the standard market architecture frameworks (e.g., TOGAF, ArchiMate, BIZBOK or equivalent) are considered strong assets.

Experience

Minimum 15 years of experience in technology, business architecture, enterprise architecture, strategy, business transformation, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership role with team-management responsibilities;
Extensive experience developing and implementing enterprise architecture frameworks, business capability models, operating models, and strategic technology roadmaps.
Advanced proficiency across enterprise, business, and solution architecture, with the ability to operate effectively at every level while maintaining a strategic perspective.
Experience applying architecture principles and governance to complex organizational challenges.
Strong understanding of business process management, organizational design, capability-based planning, and information management.
Experience working across multiple business functions and technology domains.
Proven ability to influence senior executives and facilitate decision-making among diverse stakeholder groups.
Demonstrated experience evaluating emerging technologies, including AI, and translating their potential business value into actionable technology transformation recommendations.

Show more

Show less

Seniority level

Director

Employment type

Full-time

Industries

Higher Education
